case_title: State of Punjab v. Jagtar Singh and Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; IPC s.304 Part-I r/w s.34
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Converted conviction to s.304 Part-I r/w s.34 and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for five years
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused persons were alleged to have killed their sister and her lover by strangulation due to the sister having sexual relations with the lover. The bodies of the deceased were found in the courtyard of the accused's house. An eyewitness claimed to have seen the accused taking the lover away on the pretext of serving him liquor. The prosecution also presented a post-mortem report indicating the presence of semen in the victim's vaginal swabs, suggesting possible sexual intercourse. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 of the IPC, while the High Court, based on the post-mortem report, concluded that the accused acted out of grave and sudden provocation, thereby reducing the conviction to Section 304 Part-I of the IPC. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, finding no error in disbelieving the eyewitness account and affirming the conviction under Section 304 Part-I.
